changes_made.explanation: Removed dataset/model variations that were duplicates or internal implementation details. Consolidated PubMed-Patients to PubMed-Patient. Kept only core models and datasets.
Normalized ROUGE-L to ROUGE base form. Removed 'Count of Reconstructed PIIs' as it's an experimental measurement rather than a standard NLG metric.
No LLM-as-judge evaluation used in this paper. The paper focuses on privacy attacks and metrics, not LLM-based evaluation.
No human evaluation mentioned in the paper. Evaluation is entirely automatic using perplexity and ROUGE metrics.

overall_notes: This paper focuses on privacy implications of retrieval-based language models rather than traditional NLG evaluation. The main NLG task is language modeling with next-token prediction. Evaluation is primarily through automatic metrics (perplexity and ROUGE) to measure privacy leakage. The paper doesn't include human evaluation or LLM-as-judge evaluation.
